summary: Frontend-only verification of iteration_10 fix for 'Cannot update a component' React warning on ReelPlayer. Verified three reels at 1440x900 capturing console.error via injected wrapper (React dedupes identical warnings, so same count across loops still indicates the warning fires). RESULT: The fix as described (durationsRef + stable transformer) is present in /app/frontend/src/components/ReelPlayer.tsx (lines 118-125) but the warnings STILL fire on both /r/the-outreach-part-1 (StorytimeTemplate) and /r/myth-you-need-a-referral (MythVsFactTemplate). Behavior is unchanged and correct: typing indicator appears on storytime beats, myth/fact flips to Fact side, live comments on /r/marge-reviews-saurav still render (3 comments, zero warnings on that reel).

ui_bugs.issue: React console.error still logged: 'Cannot update a component (`StorytimeTemplate`) while rendering a different component (`ReelPlayer`). ... follow the stack trace as described in https://react.dev/link/setstate-in-render'. Reproduced on /r/the-outreach-part-1 across one+ full loop (18s capture).
Same warning on /r/myth-you-need-a-referral: 'Cannot update a component (`MythVsFactTemplate`) while rendering a different component (`ReelPlayer`)'.

action_items: The claimed root cause (useTransform recomputing when `durations` identity changes) was addressed by moving durations behind durationsRef — code is present at ReelPlayer.tsx lines 118-125. But the warning persists, so the ACTUAL render-phase setState is elsewhere. Likely suspects to investigate: (a) `useMotionValueEvent(reelProgress, 'change', ...)` at line 107-110 — if framer-motion flushes queued 'change' events synchronously during a reelProgress.set() call that happens inside render (e.g., via the RAF effect or during active/paused toggle), setBeatState will fire mid-render and the template's useSyncExternalStore subscription on beatProgress is the inner 'other' component being updated. (b) The templates' useSyncExternalStore getSnapshot derives a boolean (typing / flipped) that may return a NEW value on every subscribe, which under StrictMode or during a render-phase subscribe can trigger a setState in the child while the parent is still rendering. (c) Check if `reelProgress.set(...)` is being called inside a useLayoutEffect or during a child's render pass. Recommend: wrap the setBeatState in a queueMicrotask or move the beat-index derivation to also be a useTransform/useSyncExternalStore (purely derived) so NO setState fires from the change event at all.
critical_code_review_comments: ReelPlayer.tsx:107-110 — setBeatState inside useMotionValueEvent 'change' is the only setState that is synchronously driven by reelProgress changes. If reelProgress is ever written during render (even indirectly), this will produce exactly the observed warning. Consider deriving beatState purely via useTransform/useSyncExternalStore to eliminate any render-phase setState path.

success_rate.frontend: 33% (1 of 3 reels warning-free; behavior OK on all 3)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Use console.error wrapper via page.add_init_script to format %s templates — raw msg.text shows unformatted '%s'. React dedupes identical warnings so count==1 across a full loop still means the warning fires. /r/marge-reviews-saurav is clean (0 warnings, 3 live comments). The two failing reels: /r/the-outreach-part-1 and /r/myth-you-need-a-referral.
rca of the issue: RCA (hypothesis): The durationsRef fix stabilizes the useTransform closure, but the mid-render setState is almost certainly `setBeatState` at ReelPlayer.tsx:109, invoked from useMotionValueEvent's 'change' handler. framer-motion's change pipeline can fire synchronously from within a .set() call; if any .set() on reelProgress happens inside a render path (child mount effect running sync in some paths, or a parent-driven update that writes before commit), setBeatState executes while a child template is mid-render — exactly the warning text. The templates (which subscribe to beatProgress via useSyncExternalStore) are the 'other component' being updated because framer's change event also publishes beatProgress; the child's subscriber then calls its own setState during the parent's render phase. Mitigation: derive beat index via useTransform (pure) and expose it as a motion value; let templates subscribe via useSyncExternalStore so there is NO React setState on the change path at all.
